# action.docker_plugin_push

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Pushes a local plugin to its registry, like `docker plugin push` (`POST /plugins/{name}/push`), using the provider's `registry_auth` credentials for the plugin's registry. The pushed digest is reported as `digest`.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_plugin_push.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_plugin_push" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_plugin_push.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_plugin_push.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | required |  |  | Name of the local plugin to push, e.g. `registry.example.com/org/myplugin:1.0`; the registry is taken from it. |
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |

## Example

```terraform
resource "terraform_data" "plugin_version" {
  input = "1.0"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_plugin_push.myplugin]
    }
  }
}

# Pushes the locally created plugin when its version changes. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_plugin_push.myplugin
action "docker_plugin_push" "myplugin" {
  config {
    name        = "registry.example.com/org/myplugin:${terraform_data.plugin_version.input}"
    result_path = "${path.module}/.plugin/push.json"
  }
}
```
